title: Player: Play button stops after a moment and any rerender resets position to 0 (exposed by lt-xlr)
description:
## Reported by Janusz, 2026-10-14 (main 5764c9f, Docker stack)
1. Clicking the app's Play button plays for a fraction of a second, then stops. Space plays normally.
2. Clicking a transcript word (or anything that rerenders) resets the seek slider and the video to 0.

## Reproduced (agent, real Chrome via CDP, fixture media)
A real click on .player-play logs: video#1 play/playing at 0.01 s, then video#1 pause 8 ms later, then video#2 loadstart. Final state: paused, t=0, label Play.

## Root cause [code]
- The Play button handler calls rerenderApp (controls.ts renderPlayerControls). rerenderApp rebuilds the video stage (lt-2zm), so a NEW <video> is created and the playing one is detached.
- The detached element fires 'pause'. stage.ts's pause listener sets model.player.isPlaying=false with no isCurrentVideo() guard, so the new element's loadedmetadata never resumes.
- The new element never restores model.player.currentTimeMs, so every rebuild starts at 0. That is symptom 2.
- Space works because lt-xlr removed its rerender. Before lt-xlr the same defects existed, but native controls (which play without a rerender) masked them; removing native controls made the custom Play button the only one.
- The lt-xlr live check missed this: playback was started with Space, and seek/mute were exercised while paused.

## Fix (minimal; lt-2zm stays the structural fix)
- Play button: toggle and sync the label in place, with no rerender, like Space.
- play/pause/timeupdate listeners ignore events from a replaced/detached video (isCurrentVideo guard).
- A rebuilt video restores currentTime from model.player.currentTimeMs (on loadedmetadata, before resuming play) and resumes if isPlaying.
- Opening the capture form pauses playback explicitly. That keeps today's observable behaviour on word click (it stopped, though by accident), so the learner can type a meaning.
acceptance_criteria: Real Chrome: clicking Play plays continuously and Pause pauses. Clicking a transcript word mid-video keeps the video and slider at the same position (paused for capture). A rerender while playing (e.g. speed change) keeps playing from the same position. Regression tests fail on 5764c9f and pass after the fix. Full verification green.
close_reason: Merged to main at 9906278 (branch @ 396a545; merged tree = verified branch tree). Cause: the Play click called rerenderApp, which rebuilt the <video> (lt-2zm); the detached element's 'pause' set isPlaying=false, and nothing restored the position. Fix: togglePlaybackInPlace is shared by Play and Space (no rerender); play/pause/timeupdate are guarded by isCurrentVideo(); loadedmetadata restores model.player.currentTimeMs (clamped to the video duration, else the model duration) and resumes if playing; a rejected play() resets the state; openCapture pauses. Review CHANGES-REQUIRED: rejected play, NaN clamp and test gaps fixed. The reported major (saved-occurrence jump restoring a stale time) did not reproduce: saved.ts:113 already sets currentTimeMs, and a new test confirms the jump lands at the occurrence start. 11 tests; 5 red on 5764c9f, and the rejected-play/NaN tests red on the pre-review fix. Live Chrome (Docker, Play BUTTON): plays continuously on one element; Pause works; a speed change while playing keeps playing; a word click while playing pauses at the same position with Meaning focused; a word click while paused keeps 1.3 s across a rebuilt element. Verification: tsc, build, vitest 1539 passed / 1 skipped (2 runs), no-network 5/5, privacy scan ok, host harnesses OK. Structural fix remains lt-2zm.

title: Make every transcript word clickable, with or without word timings
description:
## Finding
Word-level click→Selection panel (the good collect path, app.ts:2659-2674 `timed-word`) exists only when a cue has `wordTimings` from WhisperX alignment. Plain SRT import — the common case — renders cue text as a flat string; the only gesture is drag-select. "Watch and collect" should not depend on an optional alignment step.

## Target behaviour
- Every cue renders its `tokenizeCueText(cue.text)` tokens as inline buttons (same class/style as `timed-word`; rename the class to `cue-word` with `timed-word` kept as an alias for one release if tests reference it). Punctuation/whitespace rendered as plain text nodes between buttons.
- Click → `model.selection` for that single token (kind 'lexeme') → Selection panel focused on Meaning (the lt-cms path).
- Shift+click a second word in the same cue → extends to a phrase selection [first..second]. Keyboard: Arrow keys move between word buttons inside a cue; Shift+Arrow extends. Announce with aria-pressed on selected words.
- When `wordTimings` exist, additionally: current-word highlight during playback and click-to-seek-to-word on Alt+click (keep existing behaviour but do not make it the primary click; collecting is primary).
- Drag-select still works and now resolves to the same token range (lt-cms).

## Implementation
1. In the cue row renderer (views/player.ts after lt-939), replace the two code paths (timed vs untimed) with one token renderer that takes optional timings.
2. `tokenizeCueText` must return stable char offsets; selection uses charStart/charEnd so existing saved-item occurrence math (model.ts) is unchanged.
3. Performance: cue list rerenders on every rerenderApp; keep per-cue DOM cheap (no per-token event listeners — one delegated listener on the transcript container, read `data-token-index`).
4. Tests: SRT fixture without timings → words are buttons; click → selection; Shift+click → phrase; aligned fixture → highlight still tracks playback.
acceptance_criteria: With the plain synthetic SRT fixture, clicking any word in the transcript opens the Save form for that word; Shift+click selects a phrase; keyboard-only user can select a word; aligned fixtures keep playback highlighting. Tests pass; delta row added to the UX audit.
close_reason: Merged to main (e5b69d2; branch @ ca73f19, merged tree equals the verified branch tree, which includes lt-cfh). Every cue word is a span.cue-word[role=button]; timed words also carry .timed-word. Words have no tabindex at rest: in real Chrome, a mousedown on a focusable element blocks native text selection, as found by live CDP drags. Keyboard access goes through the cue row: Tab focuses the row, Arrow keys enter and move between words, Shift+Arrow extends, Enter/Space captures, and Esc returns to the row; this also removes the doubled Tab stops. Click captures a lexeme (Meaning focused). Shift+click extends to a phrase. Alt+click seeks on timed words. Click and drag share one tokenizer (cueWordTokens), and one delegated listener handles all words. The current-word highlight uses a half-open interval. Reviews: CHANGES-REQUIRED (tokenizer mismatch, drag regression risk, double capture, dblclick, inclusive highlight); all fixed. Live Chrome on the Docker stack: a real drag across words selected 'to jest lokalny' -> phrase capture with Meaning focused; a click captured 'test'; Tab/row -> ArrowRight x2 -> Enter captured 'to'; 0 words carry tabindex at rest. Verification: tsc, build, vitest 1501 passed / 1 skipped in 2 logged runs, no-network 5/5, privacy scan ok, host Python harnesses OK. Follow-up not done: Shift-selection grows but cannot shrink.

title: Split app.ts into per-view modules with zero behavior change
description:
## Why first
apps/web/src/app.ts is ~4,500 lines in one file; seven lt-dlf children edit it and BEADS.md requires separate worktrees per concurrent task. Without a split, every merge is a conflict. This is a mechanical move, done BEFORE any UX child starts.

## Target layout (names are suggestions; keep whatever grep-stable ids/classes tests use)
- `apps/web/src/shell.ts` — renderApp, renderHeader/nav/footer, sync banner, rerenderApp, installGlobalKeyboardShortcuts, focus-continuity helpers (requestFocusAfterRender etc.).
- `apps/web/src/views/player.ts` — renderVideoStage, renderPlayerControls, transcript workbench (cue rows, timed-word, selection panel, saveSelection UI).
- `apps/web/src/views/library.ts` — renderLibraryView + renderTranscriptLifecyclePanel.
- `apps/web/src/views/saved.ts`, `views/review.ts`, `views/practice.ts`, `views/exportImport.ts`, `views/settings.ts`.
- `apps/web/src/ui/` — shared bits: renderStatusToken, appendSourceDisclosure, formatTimeMs/formatDueAt, button helpers.
- `app.ts` becomes a thin re-export so existing imports in tests keep working (`export * from './shell'` etc.) — or update test imports in the same change; either way tests must not be weakened.

## Rules
- No behavior change: `git diff --stat` should be nearly all moves; use `git mv`-style history where possible. No renames of exported functions, DOM ids, data-* hooks or class names.
- Circular imports: views import from shell/ui/model, never from each other; shell imports views. If a view calls rerenderApp, pass it in or import from shell (shell must then not import that view at module top-level — use a registry object or dynamic import). Document the chosen pattern in a 5-line comment in shell.ts.
- `npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build` identical counts before/after; paste both.
- Do the same for model.ts ONLY if it is trivially separable (e.g. move localService sync into `model/localService.ts`); otherwise leave it and note the size.

## Steps
1. `wc -l apps/web/src/*.ts`; `grep -c "^export function" apps/web/src/app.ts`.
2. Move view by view, running typecheck after each.
3. Update lt-dlf children's file:line citations? NO — leave the beads; instead append a note on this issue mapping old app.ts line ranges → new files so citations remain resolvable.
acceptance_criteria: app.ts ≤ 200 lines (re-exports/bootstrap only); each view module ≤ 900 lines; tests/typecheck/build counts unchanged; line-range → file map posted in the issue note.
close_reason: Merged to main at 6cba904 via f3b951a (branch work/lt-939-split @ 1ccb194). app.ts is now a 2-line re-export, and the largest module is views/library.ts at 831 lines. Line-range map, old app.ts@35040d7 -> new: 5-11,161-228,1412-1662 -> ui/common.ts; 123-160,229-362,1399-1411,4449-4519 -> appShell.ts; 363-494 -> ui/snippets.ts; 495-894 -> views/practice.ts; 895-1398 -> views/exportImport.ts; 1663-1865,1913-2231 -> views/player/stage.ts; 1866-1912 -> ui/mediaConflict.ts; 2232-2693 -> views/player/controls.ts; 2694-3004 -> views/player/transcript.ts; 3005-3179 -> ui/transcriptSources.ts; 3180-3980 -> views/library.ts; 3981-4123 -> views/saved.ts; 4124-4307 -> views/review.ts; 4308-4448 -> views/settings.ts. Test count is unchanged at 1431 passed / 1 skipped, before and after. Independent review: PASS. A script diff of every top-level declaration showed only the 4 declared changes (relative import paths, plus the clearPendingMediaNameConflict setter at 2 sites). No TDZ risk in the appShell<->views cycle.

title: Qualify reload persistence in a real browser on the Docker stack
description:
## Scope
Independent real-browser qualification of epic lt-ddy (JSDOM receipts are not browser receipts — BEADS.md §Amendment closure). Run by an actor that did not implement the children. Do NOT use real learner state; use a fresh Docker project with isolated volumes.

## Procedure (record each step with a screenshot or exact DOM/IDB readback)
1. `docker compose -p lt-ddy-qual up -d --build` with a scratch LINGOTORTE_MEDIA_DIR containing only the synthetic fixture.
2. Open http://127.0.0.1:5173 in Chrome AND Firefox (showOpenFilePicker is Chromium-only; Firefox must degrade to the relink path, not error).
3. Unpaired path: Library → Choose video (persistent handle, Chrome) / Import copy (Firefox) + both .srt → Player → Save sentence… with meaning → Review shows 1 card. F5. EXPECT: Saved sentence present, transcript present, Review card present, video plays (Chrome: ≤1 permission click; Firefox: relink placeholder with the file name). Settings never opened. Record `indexedDB.databases()` and the cache record's keys (assert no `capability`).
4. Paired path: pair via `docker compose -p lt-ddy-qual exec -it api node scripts/pair-local.ts`; connect; autosave is on by default; save another sentence; observe lastSavedAt update. F5. EXPECT: reload hydrates from cache; connecting (manually, or automatically if lt-cfh is done) shows NO Keep/Load prompt because cache == last ack; service revision unchanged.
5. Divergence path: with the tab unpaired, edit (save a word) → F5 → pair/connect. EXPECT: Keep/Load prompt appears (edits newer than last ack); choose Keep → Save now → revision advances; choose Load (in a second run) → cache overwritten with service state.
6. Service restart path: `docker compose restart api` → tab shows disconnected on next action; cache still hydrates on F5.
7. `docker compose -p lt-ddy-qual down -v` at the end; confirm no files were written under the media dir.

## Report
docs/dev/lt-ddy-reload-qualification-<date>.md with image/revision hashes, browser versions, the exact steps, and any deviations. Open follow-up beads for failures; do not fix inline.
acceptance_criteria: Steps 3–6 pass in Chrome and the degraded path passes in Firefox; report committed; epic lt-ddy acceptance met.
close_reason: Report committed at docs/dev/lt-ddy-reload-qualification-2026-10-15.md (84e7ce2). Chrome steps 1-4 pass (unpaired reload restore without Settings; paired reload with no Keep/Load; divergence Keep and Load both correct; service restart -> disconnected, cache restores, pairing forgotten). Firefox degraded path passes. Cache keys contain no capability; pairing is in its own DB. Run by a non-implementer (Janusz); recorded by the agent. Follow-ups (not fixed inline, per the issue): lt-ddy.3 (P1, recommended picker ignores subtitles), lt-ddy.4 (P2, Firefox relink dead end). Gap: browser versions and the step-5 media-dir check were not reported.

title: Restore the browser media handle at boot, independent of the local service
description:
## Finding
persistence-audit Gate 4 [code]. `restoreBrowserMediaHandle` (model.ts:1415) is only invoked from inside `connectLocalService` (model.ts:440) and from the relink placeholder button (app.ts:1944). main.ts:9-11 documents this. So even though the FileSystemHandle is in IndexedDB and needs no service, playback cannot come back on reload until the pairing ritual is done.

## Target behaviour
After lt-0zc hydrates the cached snapshot, if `handleNameFromMedia(model)` is non-null, attempt `restoreBrowserMediaHandle(model)` immediately at boot:
- `queryPermission({mode:'read'})` === 'granted' → silent restore, Player plays.
- 'prompt' → do NOT call requestPermission at boot (needs a user gesture; Chromium throws otherwise). Show the existing relink placeholder (renderRelinkPlaceholder app.ts:1913) with its button text "Reconnect <filename>" which calls requestPermission inside the click handler then restores. (Verify the existing button already does this; if yes this task only wires the boot-time query path.)
- 'denied' / no handle / name mismatch → existing error copy in model.ts:1437-1456 stays.

## Implementation
1. Export a `restoreMediaAtBoot(model)` from model.ts that performs the query-only path; call it from main.ts after cache hydration and before first render (await it; it is fast).
2. Keep the SHA-256 content check (model.ts:1472-1474) — it is what makes relink-by-content safe.
3. Do not touch connectLocalService; its restore call remains for the service-hydration case.

## Tests
JSDOM with a fake handle store: granted → objectUrl set before render; prompt → relink placeholder rendered with Reconnect button, clicking calls requestPermission then sets objectUrl; denied → error copy.
acceptance_criteria: Import via "Choose video (persistent handle)" → F5 → video plays with at most one permission click and no Settings interaction. Tests pass.
close_reason: Merged to main at bc080c5 (branch work/lt-aot-media-boot @ 58e6534). restoreMediaAtBoot runs query-only, so it never calls requestPermission at boot. It is bounded at 1.5s and called from main.ts after bootSnapshotCache. A 'prompt' state shows a 'Reconnect <file>' button that requests permission on click. The SHA-256 content check is kept and connectLocalService is untouched. Review: PASS; minors applied (revoke replaced object URLs, aria-label, tests for late completion, missing queryPermission, changed file, no dirty flag). 9 tests in lt-aotMediaBoot.test.ts. Joined-tree verification as for lt-y1s. UNQUALIFIED / requires human verification: the real file picker flow ('Choose video (persistent handle)' -> F5 -> plays with at most one click) cannot be automated here; added to Janusz's checklist.

title: Cache the LocalStoreSnapshot in IndexedDB and hydrate it before first render
description:
## Finding
persistence-audit Gate 1+3 [observed+code]. All learner state lives only in `AppModel` memory. `main.ts:12-14` builds an empty model and renders; nothing browser-side persists it (grep localStorage|indexedDB in apps/web/src finds only browserHandleStore.ts, which stores a file handle, not state). Reload = empty app unless the Settings pairing ritual is repeated.

## Design
A browser-side crash/reload buffer, NOT a second source of truth:
- New module `apps/web/src/browserSnapshotCache.ts` using the same IndexedDB database as browserHandleStore (`lingotorte-handle-store`, bump DB_VERSION to 2, add object store `snapshots`) or a sibling DB — pick one and document. Keys: `'current'` → `{ schemaVersion, savedAt (model.clock()), snapshot: LocalStoreSnapshot, currentMediaId, targetTrackId, nativeTrackId, localService: { baseUrl, autosaveEnabled } }`. NEVER include the pairing capability, `pendingCueEdits`, or anything from `pairedTransport` (contract A28).
- Write: debounce 500 ms after every `markUnsavedBrowserEdits` (model.ts:515) and after every successful `saveModelToLocalService` ack (model.ts:358-366). Use structured clone of `model.store.snapshot()`; do not JSON.stringify (size/perf).
- Read on boot: in main.ts, `await readSnapshotCache()` BEFORE `createAppModel()`/first render; if present and `schemaVersion` matches, call `projectHydratedSnapshotIntoModel(model, cached.snapshot)` (model.ts:270 — export it) and restore targetTrackId/nativeTrackId/localService prefs. Then set `model.localService.syncState = 'unsaved'` with lastMessage "Restored from this browser's cache; not yet confirmed by the local service." so the existing banner is truthful.
- Reconcile with the service: when the user later connects, the EXISTING dirty-connect comparison (model.ts:420-431) will see a non-empty browser snapshot. Set `owner.baseline` from the cache's last service-acked snapshot (store `lastAckedSerialized` in the cache when a save acks) so that an unchanged cache does NOT trigger the Keep/Load choice prompt — only genuinely newer edits do.
- Clear: on "Load service state (discard browser edits)" (resolveLocalServiceConnection model.ts:477-487) overwrite the cache with the service snapshot. Provide `clearSnapshotCache()` and a Settings button "Clear this browser's cached state" (secondary, with confirm).
- Failure handling: every IDB call wrapped; on any error log once to console and continue without cache (never block render).

## Tests (vitest + fake-indexeddb, add dev dep if absent — note it in the issue)

title: Create a recognition review card automatically on every save
description:
## Finding
ux-audit Task C [observed+code]. Saved items do not become review cards. Each one needs a manual "Create review card" click in the Saved view (app.ts:4104-4116), which also only ever uses `occurrences[0]`. With no meaning entered, the card's front (`Recognize: ${displayText}`, model.ts:3108) and back are the same sentence.

## Target behaviour
- Saving an occurrence (the unified path from lt-cms) also creates ONE recognition card for the saved item if none exists yet (idempotent per savedItem.id, not per occurrence). FSRS state starts as 'new'.
- The Saved view button becomes a toggle: "In review ✓" (click → archive the card, not delete) / "Add to review" for items that were opted out. Bulk control at the top of each Saved tab: "Add all to review (N)".
- When `meaning` is empty, the recognition card back shows the native cue line as the answer (already done when a native track exists, app.ts:4197-4202); when neither exists, the Saved view and the Review reveal show an inline "Add meaning" input that writes `savedItem.meaning` and persists (persistIfLocalServiceAutosaveEnabled).

## Implementation
1. model.ts: find `createReviewCardForSavedItem` and `saveSelection`; after a successful save, call `ensureReviewCardForSavedItem(model, item, occurrence)` which returns early if a non-archived card already references the item (check `model.store.snapshot().reviewCards` by savedItemId).
2. Respect `lt-2rl` injectable clock (`model.clock()`), never `Date.now()`.
3. Audit/migration: a new card is a normal reviewCards insert — no schema change. If the store has a forward-migration pattern (lt-f5h), confirm none is needed and say so in the note.
4. Review view stats line (app.ts:4269-4273) currently prints `due: <ISO UTC>`; format with `formatDueAt` in the learner's locale (it exists — check its output) and move state/due behind a `<details>` "scheduling" disclosure.

## Tests
JSDOM: save → exactly one card exists; second save of same item → still one; toggle off archives; "Add all" creates cards only for items lacking one; review of a meaning-less item shows native line or Add-meaning input.
acceptance_criteria: After `lt-cms` + this: Library fixture → Save sentence… → Save → Review shows 1 due card with no further clicks; repeated saves never duplicate cards; tests pass; Delta row for Task C.
close_reason: Merged to main (17518b3; branch work/lt-uzo-auto-card @ 7407e16, merged tree equals the verified branch tree). saveSelection now creates one recognition card per saved item in the same synchronous step (FSRS 'new', model.clock()), idempotent per savedItem.id. Archiving uses the existing ReviewCard.suspendedAt, which needs no schema change or migration and keeps the card, its state and its events; toggling back reactivates the same card. 'Add all to review (N)' is hidden at 0. Add meaning appears when there is neither a meaning nor a native line. Scheduling sits behind a <details>, and the deck count excludes archived cards with '(N archived)'. Review: PASS; minors applied (active-only count, earliest occurrence for re-add, required meaning input, no-op archive skips persist), plus a new test. title: Unify the collect gesture: one capture card, no save-on-mouseup
description:
## Finding
ux-audit H4/H5 + Task B [code]. Three ways to collect produce three different outcomes:
- `timed-word` click (app.ts:2659-2674) → sets `model.selection` → Selection panel with Meaning/Notes form (renderSelectionPanel app.ts:2910-3003) → explicit Save occurrence. GOOD, but only exists when word timings exist.
- Drag-select text in a cue row → `mouseup` handler (app.ts:2844-2881) calls `saveSelectedPhraseFromCue` IMMEDIATELY: no confirm, no meaning, no undo. An accidental drag creates a vocab item.
- `Save sentence` button (app.ts:2773-2790) → `saveSentenceFromCue` immediately, no meaning. The resulting review card then has an empty answer side (see lt-… auto-card task).

## Target behaviour
Every collect gesture leads to the SAME capture state: `model.selection = {kind, text, cueId, tokenStart, tokenEnd, charStart, charEnd}` and the Selection panel is shown with the Meaning input focused. Nothing is persisted until "Save occurrence" (or Enter in the Meaning field). Esc / Cancel clears the selection.

## Implementation
1. mouseup handler (app.ts:2844-2881): keep the tokenize + token-matching logic, but instead of calling `saveSelectedPhraseFromCue`, build the selection object (kind: 'lexeme' if one token matched, else 'phrase') and assign it to `model.selection`; then `requestFocusAfterRender(model, 'selection-meaning')` and `rerenderApp`.
2. `Save sentence` click (app.ts:2780-2789): set `model.selection = { kind:'sentence', text: cue.text, cueId: cue.id, tokenStart:0, tokenEnd: <token count>, charStart:0, charEnd: cue.text.length }`, focus meaning, rerender. Rename the button label to "Save sentence…" (ellipsis = opens a form).
3. In renderSelectionPanel: Enter in `#selection-meaning` triggers the same path as the Save occurrence button; Esc anywhere in the form = Cancel. Reuse `saveSelection(model)` (already handles kinds via model.ts) — verify it handles kind 'sentence' identically to `saveSentenceFromCue`; if not, route by kind inside saveSelection.
4. Keep `saveSelectedPhraseFromCue`/`saveSentenceFromCue` exported for tests but no UI path may call them directly.
5. The draft-transcript gate (`canSaveFromTargetTrack`, app.ts:2726) still applies: when the track is not approved, the Save occurrence button is disabled with the existing title text.

## Tests
Update/add JSDOM tests in tests/ for: drag-select creates a selection and does NOT create a saved item; Save sentence opens the form; Enter in meaning saves with the meaning; Esc cancels; draft track blocks save.
acceptance_criteria: No code path persists a saved item without the Selection panel having been shown; all three gestures end in the same form with Meaning focused; tests listed above pass; Delta rows for H4/H5 and Task B in ux-audit §5.

Five gestures, all through ui/capture.ts openCapture: timed-word click, drag-select, 'Save sentence…', subtitle-overlay word ('Capture X'), and timed-word on approved tracks. Each shows the Selection panel with Meaning focused. Nothing persists until Save occurrence or Enter in Meaning; Esc cancels. The draft-track gate is kept, and a refused drag-select now shows 'Approve the transcript before saving from it.' Sentences carry their meaning (saveSelection 'sentence' path matches saveSentenceFromCue field by field). Drag-select is anchored by Range offsets. title: Style every class emitted by app.ts that has no rule in style.css
description:
## Finding
ux-audit V1/V3/V4/V5 [code+observed]. ~50 class names set via `className =` in app.ts / morphologyPanel.ts have no selector in style.css, so Review, Saved tabs, Practice, Export/Import and timed-word buttons render as browser defaults (white UA buttons, black-on-dark text, no spacing). Full list: ux-audit Appendix A. Regenerate with:
```
cd apps/web/src
grep -oE "className = ['\`]([a-z0-9-]+)" app.ts morphologyPanel.ts | sed -E "s/.*= ['\`]//" | sort -u > /tmp/used.txt
grep -oE "^\.[a-z0-9-]+" style.css | sed 's/^\.//' | sort -u > /tmp/styled.txt
comm -23 /tmp/used.txt /tmp/styled.txt
```

## Rules (do not improvise a new look)
- Use ONLY existing tokens from `:root` in style.css (--surface, --surface-raised, --border, --text-muted, --accent, --radius, etc.). No new colors, no new fonts.
- Reuse existing patterns: tabs → copy `.lingotorte-nav button` pill style for `.saved-tab` with `[aria-selected="true"]` as the active state; chips → `.status-token` for `.bucket-chip`; secondary buttons → `.btn-secondary` for `.review-controls button`, `.practice-controls button`, `.button-row button`; inline word buttons `.timed-word` → copy `.subtitle-word` (transparent, inherit font, hover background) so transcript text reads as text.
- `.meta`, `.file-hint`, `.occurrence-link` are styled only under `.saved-item` — promote them to top-level rules with the same values.
- Group the new rules by view in style.css with a comment header per view (`/* Review */`, `/* Saved */`, `/* Practice */`, `/* Export / Import */`, `/* Transcript workbench */`).
- Every rule must be ≤ 6 declarations; this is a gap-fill, not a redesign (typography/hierarchy is a separate task).

## Steps
1. Run the comm command; paste output in the issue note as the "before" list.
2. Add rules until the command prints nothing except intentionally unstyled semantic hooks (document any you leave, with reason).
3. Walk Player, Library, Saved (both tabs), Review (before/after reveal), Practice (each mode), Export/Import, Settings at 1280×800 and 390×844; attach screenshots.
4. Run the full verification contract from epic lt-dlf.

title: Fix app-shell grid: sync banner steals the 1fr row from <main>
description:
## Finding
ux-audit V2 [observed+code]. `.lingotorte-app { display:grid; grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto }` (style.css:70-77) assumes three children: header, main, footer. `renderApp` (app.ts:132-153) appends FOUR: header, `syncStatus` div (`[data-local-service-sync]`, app.ts:135-138), main, footer. Whenever the banner is not `hidden` (any unsaved state — i.e. after the first edit), it occupies the `1fr` row and `<main>` lands in an implicit `auto` row → a huge empty banner box above all content. Screenshot evidence in the audit (Saved/Review/Library views).

## Fix (pick ONE, prefer the first)
A. style.css: change to `grid-template-rows: auto auto 1fr auto;` and add `.lingotorte-app > [data-local-service-sync][hidden] { display:none }` (already covered by the global `[hidden]` rule at style.css:1133 — verify the row collapses when hidden; with `display:none` the element is not a grid item so a 3-row layout would also hold; the explicit 4-row template is still correct because the hidden element is removed from the grid).
B. app.ts: move the `syncStatus` element inside the `<header>` returned by renderHeader so the child count stays three.

Do NOT add a wrapper div around main+banner; keep the DOM contract used by tests (`[data-local-service-sync]` query selectors in app.ts:140,146 and tests/).

## Steps
1. `grep -rn "data-local-service-sync\|lingotorte-app" apps/web/src tests` to see every consumer before editing.
2. Apply the one-line change.
3. Browser: load fixture, click Save sentence (makes state dirty, banner appears), navigate to Saved and Review. The banner must be a single-line strip directly under the header; `<main>` immediately below it.
4. Mobile 390×844 check.

title: Persistence: learner state and media survive a browser reload without a ritual
description:
## Scope
Grouping epic for docs/review/persistence-audit-2026-10-13.md Option A (browser-side durability, no policy change) plus one explicit decision bead for Option B (remembered pairing). Option C (service-streamed media) is deferred under lt-5lb.

## Problem statement (verified 2026-10-13)
Reload → empty app. Live probe from http://127.0.0.1:5173: /api/health 200, /api/status 401 (unpaired), indexedDB.databases() = [], localStorage empty. Root cause is five stacked gates: (1) pairing is process-memory only and nothing connects on boot (main.ts:6-15, app.ts:4379 is the only connect caller); (2) capability obtainable only via private terminal and rotates on restart (privateDelivery.ts, docker-runbook.md:41-44); (3) autosaveEnabled defaults false and resets on pair (model.ts:175,203); (4) plain import stores a blob: originalPath that cannot survive reload (model.ts:1273-1284, needsMediaRelink model.ts:1154) and handle restore runs only inside connectLocalService (model.ts:440); (5) dirty-connect choice prompt (model.ts:424-430).

## Design principle for children
The local service stays the durable, portable store with CAS revisions (lt-8hh, lt-04i unchanged). The browser gains a crash/reload buffer: the same LocalStoreSnapshot JSON cached in IndexedDB, hydrated before first render, and reconciled with the service through the EXISTING dirty-connect comparison path. Never store the pairing capability under this epic (see lt-9zj contract line 120; changing that is lt-… decision bead only).

## Boundaries and closure
Scope per lt-chi. Synthetic fixtures and isolated stores only. No real learner-state replacement. Preserve docs/dev/local-request-authenticity-contract.md invariants A28 (nothing secret in web storage). Record exact revision/patch, tests, browser reload receipts, independent review. Parent/operator closes.

title: Decision: state the single-operator threat model and simplify ceremony accordingly
description:
## Question for Janusz (product/privacy tradeoff)
The pairing-via-private-TTY design, capability rotation on restart, zero-side-effect rejection and "never in browser storage" rules (lt-9zj, lt-sor, docs/dev/local-request-authenticity-contract.md) defend against hostile LAN peers and other users of the same machine. The stated user is one person on one laptop. The two are in tension and it resurfaces in every persistence/convenience decision (lt-z41 is the first; service-streamed media lt-zt0 will be the next).

## Options
A. **Single trusted operator, single trusted machine.** The private LAN is a convenience, not a trust boundary. Consequences: pairing can be remembered (lt-z41 → B or C), the capability may be minted once to a file the browser can read, Origin/Host checks stay (they are cheap and stop drive-by web pages), TTY-only delivery becomes optional. Hosted/multi-user remains explicitly out of scope.
B. **Keep the current model.** Other LAN devices and same-machine users are adversaries. Consequences: lt-z41 → A (re-pair every reload), lt-zt0 needs its own admission design, all future convenience work carries this cost. Document that the cost is accepted.
C. **Tiered**: A on the laptop (loopback), B when `LINGOTORTE_BIND` is a LAN address. Adds a config switch and two test matrices.

## Recommendation (agent, non-binding)
A, written as one paragraph in DECISIONS.md and referenced from safety-privacy-boundary-review.md. It does not remove any existing control; it stops requiring new work to defend against adversaries that are not in the product's scope.

## Closure
Janusz closes with the option in notes; DECISIONS.md entry in the same commit. lt-z41 and lt-zt0 cite this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Closed with option named and DECISIONS.md updated; lt-z41 re-evaluated against it.
close_reason: Janusz chose option A (single trusted operator, single trusted machine) on 2026-10-13 in chat. Recorded as DECISIONS.md §14 with a pointer added to docs/review/safety-privacy-boundary-review.md, both in the same commit. No existing control is removed. lt-z41 remains its own decision and is now judged against this threat model.

title: Stop rebuilding the video stage on every rerender
description:
## Finding
`rerenderApp` discards the whole DOM and reconstructs it on every state change — each keystroke in transcript search, each Save, each speed change. The `<video>` is recreated and re-`src`'d each time (renderVideoStage). Symptoms: playback hiccups/position resets, lost focus (lt-r4k.2 was a workaround), and the re-render loop class of bug (lt-r4k.4). The toast (lt-e0j) and sticky transcript (lt-vtw) will fight this too.

## Decision (record in the issue note)
Option 1 — minimal, fits current style: mount the video stage ONCE. Keep a module-level `stageEl`/`videoEl`; `renderVideoStage` returns the existing element and only updates attributes that changed (src only when mediaId/objectUrl changed; playbackRate; loop flags). Subtitle overlay and controls remain re-rendered children but are appended into the persistent stage. Wrap in a small `keyed(el, key, create, update)` helper so the same trick can be reused for the toast region and the transcript list later.
Option 2 — adopt a tiny diffing renderer (lit-html or Preact, ~4–10 KB, vendored to respect the no-network/local-only policy). Bigger change; only pick if Option 1 proves leaky.

## Steps (Option 1)
1. Identify every `document.createElement('video')` and `src =` site; there should be one after this.
2. Ensure `timeupdate`/`ended`/`error` listeners are attached once (idempotent install), not per render.
3. Tests: render twice with same media → same `HTMLVideoElement` instance and no second `src` assignment; media change → new src; playback position preserved across a Save (JSDOM: assert currentTime untouched).
4. Browser check: play fixture, type in transcript search while playing — no stutter, no position jump; verify lt-r4k.4 regression test still passes.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one video element lifetime per media selection; playback continues uninterrupted across saves/search/speed changes; existing focus-continuity and media-error tests pass; keyed-element helper documented for reuse.
close_reason: Decision: Option 1 (mount once, no renderer dependency). Merged to main at 74e539d (branch @ 743f9d4; merged tree = verified tree). ui/keyed.ts keyed(model, slot, key, create, update, release) is a per-model WeakMap cache, documented for reuse (toast lt-e0j, transcript list). The stage is keyed by media id + playback URL: src is set once, listeners are attached once and read state at event time; updates refresh only rate, label, overlay and alert; a media change releases the old element (pause, remove src, load). rerenderApp builds the new root first, then replaceChild (the same-task reinsert avoids Chrome's removal pause), with a resume net when isPlaying && paused. title: Decision: remember the service pairing across reloads (amends lt-9zj contract)
description:
## Question for Janusz (scope/privacy tradeoff — not a technical decision an agent may make)
docs/dev/local-request-authenticity-contract.md line 120 and invariant A28 (accepted under lt-9zj) say the capability is kept in memory only and "Reload requires pairing again"; line 43 records this cost knowingly. persistence-audit Gate 1+2 shows that for a single learner on one laptop this cost is the main reason the app feels amnesiac even after lt-0zc/lt-aot/lt-4ji land (state will come back, but nothing durable is written until the learner re-pairs via terminal).

## Options
A. Keep contract as is. Learner re-pairs after every reload. (Status quo; no work.)
B. `sessionStorage` only: capability survives F5 but not tab/window close; auto-connect at boot when present; 401 → clear and fall back to Settings. Rotation on service restart unchanged. Threat delta: same-origin script in the same tab (already fatal under the contract's "trusted browser" assumption); other tabs/profiles unaffected.
C. IndexedDB with explicit opt-in checkbox "Remember this pairing on this device until the service restarts". Survives tab close. Threat delta: any same-origin script in the profile, and disk persistence of the secret on the host.
D. Replace bearer capability with a browser-held, origin-bound credential (e.g. WebAuthn/PRF or an HttpOnly cookie minted once by the terminal helper). Larger; would retire the pairing field entirely. Out of this epic's budget — note for lt-5lb if interesting.

## Recommendation (agent, non-binding)
B. It removes the F5 ritual at the smallest threat delta and keeps restart-rotation. Record as a DECISIONS.md entry and amend contract line 120 + A28 wording to "sessionStorage permitted; never localStorage/IndexedDB/snapshot/export/logs".

## Closure
Janusz closes with the chosen option in notes. If B or C: lt-… (implement remembered pairing) becomes ready. If A: close that implementation bead as won't-do.

title: Subtitle overlay must not cover the native <video controls> bar
description:
## Finding
ux-audit V6/V7 [observed+code]. `renderVideoStage` sets `controls` on the <video> (app.ts:1718) AND the app renders its own control row (renderPlayerControls app.ts:2232-2392: Play/Prev/Next/Loop/Loop range/Speed/time). `.subtitle-overlay` is `position:absolute; bottom:0` (style.css:385-400), so the target-language subtitle sits on top of the browser's native control bar. Zoomed screenshot in the audit.

## Fix (decide and record which)
Option 1 (preferred — one source of truth): remove the `controls` attribute. The custom row already covers play/pause, cue navigation and speed. Add what the native bar had and the custom row lacks: a seek slider (`<input type=range>` bound to currentTime/duration, updated on `timeupdate`, seeks on `input`), a mute toggle, and a fullscreen button (`stage.requestFullscreen()`). Keyboard: Space toggles play when focus is not in an editable field (extend installGlobalKeyboardShortcuts app.ts:229-280; the shortcuts help text at app.ts:2388 must list it).
Option 2 (minimal): keep `controls`, add `padding-bottom: 3.25rem` to `.subtitle-overlay` so cues clear the bar, and accept duplicate Play buttons. Only choose this if Option 1 breaks an existing test that cannot be reasonably updated.

Either way: `video.setAttribute('role','img')` at app.ts:1720 is wrong for an interactive video — remove it and rely on the accessible name via aria-label.

## Steps
1. `grep -rn "controls\|role.*img" apps/web/src/app.ts tests` to see test coupling.
2. Implement; verify loop/loopRange still work via `timeupdate` (app.ts:1724-1737) — they do not depend on native controls.
3. Browser: play fixture, confirm subtitle fully visible during playback and while hovering the stage; confirm seek/mute/fullscreen work; 390×844 check.
acceptance_criteria: During playback the full subtitle text is visible and no native control bar overlaps it; exactly one play/pause control is visible; seek, mute, fullscreen reachable by mouse and keyboard. Typecheck/test/build green. Delta rows for V6/V7.
close_reason: Merged to main at 599dccd (branch @ 27a2e50). Option 1: removed native controls and role=img (aria-label kept). The app's control row adds Seek (synced in place; frozen only while dragging), Mute (aria-pressed, survives stage rebuilds), and Fullscreen on .video-stage (label toggles, in-stage shortcut hint), plus Space play/pause (skipped in editable fields and focusable widgets, no rerender). Review CHANGES-REQUIRED (slider froze after seek, fullscreen label/hint, Space rerender, test gaps): all fixed; 12 tests. Live Chrome on Docker at 1280x800 and 390x844: one Play/Pause; Space plays without scrolling; Mute, Seek click and keyboard, Fullscreen enter/exit all work; overlay inside the stage with no bar under it; no horizontal overflow. A live-found missing space in the hint was fixed. title: De-jargon learner-facing copy and hide hashes/token spans behind details
description:
## Finding
ux-audit H3/V8/V9 [observed]. Learner-facing strings use implementation vocabulary and leak identifiers:
- Saved occurrence context and Review reveal print the media content hash (`m4EHdaKEAM3+…`) and "tokens 0–4 • chars 0–28" (app.ts:4095-4099, 4205).
- Labels: "object URL", "File.text()", "persistent media handle", "track v1", "lexeme", "occurrence", "Source-backed study cockpit", "Transcript co-pilot", "Study cockpit", "cue 1", "approved" (as a bare chip).
- Hero status rail shows seven lowercase chips of mixed importance (renderStudyStatusRail app.ts:1472-1517).

## Rules
- This is a copy pass: change string literals and which fields are shown; do not change data, ids, test hooks (`data-testid`, element ids) or ARIA roles. Where a test asserts on a label, update the test in the same change.
- Keep provenance available: everything removed from the primary line must remain inside the existing `appendSourceDisclosure` "details" element (app.ts:1447) so the audit trail is one click away.
- Vocabulary map (apply consistently, add to docs/product/ as `ui-vocabulary.md`):
  lexeme → word · occurrence → "saved from <video> at <time>" · cue N → "line N" · track vN → omit from primary line · approved/draft → "Transcript ready" / "Transcript draft — approve before saving words" · Study cockpit → "Player" · Transcript co-pilot → "Transcript" · Selection → "Save a word or phrase" · "Import persistent media handle" → "Choose video (stays linked after reload)" · Local service → "Local storage service".
- Status rail: keep at most 3 chips in the hero (transcript readiness, N saved, due today); move the rest (local/private, media label, study time estimate, streak) to the footer or a `<details>`.
- The Review stats line "N cards in local deck • state: new • due: <ISO UTC>" → "N cards · next due <relative, local time>" with state/ISO inside details (coordinate with lt-uzo step 4; whichever lands second adapts).

## Steps
1. `grep -n "textContent = \|placeholder = \|title = " apps/web/src/app.ts | wc -l` to size it; work view by view (Player, Library, Saved, Review, Settings).
2. For each changed string, grep tests/ for the old text.
3. Browser walkthrough of the three core tasks reading every visible string aloud: no string may mention a browser API, a hash, a version number or a token index outside a details element.
